_comment: Systems of record for the evidence gate (docs/adr/0008-evidence-gate.md). An assessment's `## Sources` row names a CLASS; independence is counted over each class's `system` (lower-cased, whitespace collapsed), so two classes with one system are one source. `counts: false` = recorded, worth zero. `live: true` marks a system where live state is kept; unless the assessment says `Live state: none — <why>`, one of its two systems must be live. `nouns` are only suggestions for source-snapshot.py; the gate never reads them. `probes` are argv lists the snapshot runs to see whether a CLI answers; a class with none is reported unknown. Edit freely: add your identity provider's CLI as a probe, split a class, add one. A class not listed here is refused, not ignored.

identity.note: users, roles, tenants, sign-in; read the provider, not the app's copy

data.note: rows, flags, counts; read-only, never write while assessing

runtime.note: behaviour, errors, timing; read the logs at the time it happened

code.note: code paths; read them at the DEPLOYED commit, not the branch tip

memory.note: rulings and traps already on record

derived.note: a value the app derived from another system; recorded, worth zero
